body: Despite that fact that I understand what you are trying to do (i.e. mock / spy a `@ConfigMapping` bean), while also being completely aware of the fact that we don't provide any real solution, the fact that it worked in previous versions was purely accidental.
@mkouba @radcortez what's the reason that the bean generated for `@ConfigMapping` is of `@Dependant` scope? These are application wide beans, so why not have them be `@ApplicationScoped`?
I'll answer my own question - it seems that this is done to support the `@ConfigProperties`, but then the question becomes, is that really something we want to support?

> the fact that it worked in previous versions was purely accidental.

Well, I was following this [blog post](https://quarkus.io/blog/overriding-configuration-from-test-code/#approach-2-mocking-the-config-with-mockito)

Yes, MP `@ConfigProperties` is specified out as a Dependant bean. Also, old `@ConfigRoot` is also Dependant.

In reality, a `@ConfigMapping` is not a CDI Bean, since the lifecycle is managed by Config and not CDI. For example, they do not support CDI interceptors. We do provide a synthetic creator for the injection convenience. I don't see an issue in making them `@ApplicaitonScoped`.

The correct way to mock config mappings is documented here: https://quarkus.io/guides/config-mappings#mocking

> Well, I was following this [blog post](https://quarkus.io/blog/overriding-configuration-from-test-code/#approach-2-mocking-the-config-with-mockito)

We'll need to update that
@gbourant okay, so it turns out that all you need to make your code work is to add `@Unremovable` to `ProjectConfig`

issue.title: Properly document how to use @InjectMock with @ConfigMapping
